145	### Core Rules
146	
147	*Conventions.* Rules are `SE-n`; formulas `D.n`; acceptance criteria `AC-SE-n`; restore reasons `SUIT_RESTORE_*`; diagnostics `suit_*`. `[PH]` marks a placeholder that is registered with a range (Tuning Knobs) and is never a fact until the pacing spike confirms it. "(provisional — X undesigned)" marks a contract with a system whose GDD does not yet exist (Interaction, Ship Section & Layout and 2D Lighting & Occlusion were formerly in flight and are now designed; their rows quote current text); "must repeat" names what that GDD has to restate (the Graph's own rule for provisional rows). "(orchestrator ruling: ...)" marks a place where two specialist proposals disagreed and the stage rulings, or failing that a stated choice, decided. The four Graph band constants appear **only by name** (`COLD_DMG_ONSET_MC`, `HEAT_DMG_ONSET_MC`, `HYPOXIA_PP`, `DECOMP_P`); Suit reads them from the registry and never restates a value (the Graph's source-lint, AC-SE-1). Every rule carries *Rule*, *Why*, *Rejected* and *Criterion*, and is tied to a pillar. 258	#### Group F — Seams
259	
260	**SE-31. No stimuli pushed.** *Rule.* Suit pushes no noise or power stimuli to Attention in the MVP. Per-verb noise class lives in **Interaction's verb declarations**; Suit keeps no noise field of its own (the earlier idea of a Suit-side noise table is withdrawn so there is one table of record). The kernel's Interactions row 4 says Suit "pushes noise/power stimuli to Attention": that wording is a routed refresh (Cross-References). The top-up is a Graph stock withdrawal; whether Attention sees it is not relied on here. *Criterion.* AC-SE-32 (no call from Suit's code to an Attention intake). *Pillar.* P3.
261	
262	**SE-32. Pause.** *Rule.* Nothing Suit registers carries `allowed_when_paused`; `equip_tool` and every mutator are rejected while paused. The Chart Table's beam-shape pick is a boot or new-game call, not a runtime command. *Rejected.* Paused equip (lets a solo player re-arm with time stopped mid-tell, against Pillar 2). *Criterion.* AC-SE-33. *Pillar.* P2.
263	
264	**SE-33. Autosave seam (adopted: Save/Load's package).** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *Rule.* Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): accept Save/Load's package (OQ-13; Save/Load OQ-40 and OQ-41; D14 and D42): (a) "any bound seat `vitals_state ≥ CRITICAL`" is a **third soft-gate input** for the autosave (deferred up to `AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS`, registry 7200, then written RISKY, invisible to the player: no glyph) and is **also applied to `quit_risky`**; (b) a **fairness step-back**: `loop_hit` also fires when `T_downed − g_r.T < W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE`, independent of `risky`; (c) a **post-DOWNED refractory** of `W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE` ticks. Save/Load owns (a)-(c) and their draft criteria AC-SL-128 and AC-SL-129, which are promoted there. *Suit's half.* Suit supplies exactly one input, `view(player_id).vitals_state` (the worst of the three persisted rungs, derived on read, never saved), and changes nothing else; a derived `time_to_failure_runs` read is **not minted** (a STRAINED-yet-doomed seat, for example 31 s of reserve and a 40 s exit, is caught by the step-back (b), not by the gate). *Derivation of the window used by (b) and (c).* `W_MIN_WARNING_S` is the registry's 10 s and `TICK_RATE` is 60, so the window is 10 × 60 = **600 ticks**. It is the Graph's own fairness floor, and Suit's `SUIT_MIN_WARNING_S` (20 s, 1,200 ticks) is at least twice it (build assertion A1). A generation written inside the final 600 ticks before a DOWNED seat's `T_downed` would restore the player with less than the minimum warning, so the step-back skips it. *Worked example.* A seat is first cued at tick t0 and is DOWNED at t0 + 1,500 (25 s, the breath floor of D.11): an autosave written at t0 + 1,000 is 500 ticks before `T_downed`, inside the window, so `loop_hit` fires and the restore steps back past it; one written at t0 + 800 is 700 ticks before and is not stepped back. The second route into a doomed restore, a data retune making every saved restore fail, is closed on Suit's side by `data_rev` (SE-34, AC-SE-49). The event autosaves for weld, cut and module-cut (D17), the assembly-breach withholding (D54) and the fault loss window (D55) are Save/Load's and Assembly's. *Criterion.* AC-SE-34a and 34b. *Pillar.* P5.
265	
266	**SE-34. Save, restore, derived values.** *Rule.* SL-15 items 1-12 apply: `supported_versions`; a plain-data `snapshot()` (no `Vector2i`, no `StringName` keys, no typed containers); a two-phase `restore` returning `(ok, reason, detail)`; **hard failure, never clamp** on an out-of-range field *(except the declared `data_rev` migration below)*; `default_state()`; `post_restore` sets every `prev_*` field to its current value (no spurious edge cue after a restore); explicit dirty keys (4.7 packed-array rule); restore-idempotent (`snapshot(restore(snapshot()))` byte-equal); PER_PLAYER keyed by PlayerId. The closed restore reasons are in SE-38. **Data revisions** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the block persists a block-level `data_rev` (the revision of `assets/data/suit/*.json`, bumped by hand for any retune of `R_BREATH`, `RESERVE_S`, `CELL_S`, `TL_MAX`, `RUNG_MIN_TICKS`, `HYPOX_FAIL_S`, `INTEG_FAIL_S` or `STAGGER_WINDOW_TICKS`), and `assets/data/suit/rev_history.json` keeps, for each past revision, the saved values of `R_BREATH`, `RESERVE_S`, `CELL_S`, `TL_MAX` and the derived hold maxima. A saved `data_rev` equal to the current one is restored strictly (an out-of-range field is `SUIT_RESTORE_FIELD_RANGE`, a defect or tampering). A saved `data_rev` **older** than the current and present in the history is a legitimate retune and is **rescaled, not failed**: `reserve_mgu` and `cell_ticks` keep their felt fraction (`new = floor(saved × RESERVE_MAX_now / RESERVE_MAX_saved)`, likewise `CELL_MAX_TICKS`), `thermal_load` and every `hold`, `rf_warmth` and `p_age` are reduced to the new maxima (the safe direction: a shorter counter only lengthens the tell), the diagnostic `suit_restore_rescaled` is emitted, and the restore succeeds. A saved `data_rev` newer than the build, or absent from the history, fails `SUIT_RESTORE_DATA_REV_UNKNOWN`. Without this path a data retune made every saved restore fail and left the player with no loadable save at the moment of death (the doomed-save risk of OQ-13's second route). The rescale is a declared migration, not a clamp; Save/Load confirms it is within SL-15 (OQ-45). **Instance decode** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*: in `post_restore` (the same place and mechanism as `SUIT_RESTORE_CARRY_MISMATCH`; Suit's `restore_after` is `[]` but `post_restore` runs after all blocks restore, CR-8) Suit decodes every held instance with `from_array(a, graph_step_no)`, `graph_step_no` being the restored Graph's absolute 10 Hz `step_no`; a wrong length or element type fails `SUIT_RESTORE_INSTANCE_FORM`, a `validate_instance` failure maps to `SUIT_RESTORE_FIELD_RANGE`, an unknown `def_id` stays `SUIT_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_DEF` and a count above `stack_max` stays `SUIT_RESTORE_STOWED_OVERFLOW`; live state is untouched and nothing is clamped. Derived values — `locomotion_cap`, `vitals_state`, cue levels, `held_mass_g`, `stowed_mass_g`, `cue_load`, the breath source — are computed on read and never saved. MVP death is restart from the last autosave: `suit.state` rolls back with the world and there is no PROFILE block in the MVP. *Criterion.* AC-SE-35 (SL-15 round trip, restore idempotence). *Pillar.* P5.
267	
268	**SE-35. External stagger, DECOMP pull, pod.** *Stagger.* The Controller registers the `SYSTEM`-origin command type `stagger {actor}` (registry `stagger`; Player Controller PC-1 b: `coalesce NONE`, `max_age_ticks` 120, no player binding, rejected `NOT_STAGGERABLE` in DOWNED, DEAD or IN_POD, Applied without extending the lock in STAGGERED); the former CONFLICT is closed, 2026-10-27. Suit submits one on a two-band pressure drop inside `STAGGER_WINDOW_TICKS` `[PH]` (dormant at MVP: no locked fixture fires it; the specified interface stays and is tested on synthetic traces; OQ-38) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, evaluated by **D.12** (the one normative statement of the trigger): the occupant's `band_p` index (NORMAL 0, LOW 1, DECOMP 2, VACUUM 3) must rise by 2 or more between a sample taken at most `STAGGER_WINDOW_TICKS` earlier and the current run, **in the same compartment**. A compartment change (a door crossing, the SE-3 NONE-to-EXPOSED switch, leaving IN_POD, the first run after a bind) re-anchors the window and never counts, so a player who walks into a vented room by choice is not input-locked for it, while a pressure fall inside the room they stand in is; one stagger per event; the two window ages are persisted (SE-38) so a restore mid-window replays the same trigger; the DECOMP cue plays as well, and a cap falling edge still staggers through the Controller's own rule. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *Pull.* Cue only (a lean, draught audio, dust); no displacement ("a stagger is animation plus input lock, never an impulse"). *Pod* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* (D60 reverses the former hold). Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): statuses run in the pod, and a death in the pod is the Controller's DEAD. While the Controller's `loco_state` is IN_POD, Suit runs the full SE-39 sequence for the seat against the pod cabin rule of SE-3 (i) (POD_RUN): **no `draw_air` call** (the pod's section is dormant and never breathed, Web Map & Transit WM-5, WM-17); the breath source is RESERVE and then NONE; the reserve drains `R_BREATH` per run; the cell drains while the beam is lit; the thermal load relaxes against COMFORT with no gain; every hold counter advances; the cap, the cues and the marks follow the ladders as anywhere. `pending_draw_mgu` is 0 in the pod, so no shortfall can arise: `breath_starved` stays 0 and no GASP cue fires across a leg (Web Map WM-17's required criterion holds by construction). A seat that reaches FAILED in the pod is DOWNED and then DEAD by the Controller's own rule (`DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS`); Suit special-cases nothing and holds nothing. What a leg costs, and when it can kill, is derived in D.1 (a nominal leg of 945 ticks spends 157 runs x 300 = 47,100 mGU, 15.7 s of the 90 s reserve, with the remainder of 3 ticks carried, so 157 or 158 runs; a pod death needs a leg of at least 250 runs, 25 s, so it is unreachable at the registry defaults) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R6)*. The `stagger` trigger cannot fire in the pod (D.12: `band_p` is NORMAL there by rule, and the Controller rejects `stagger` as `NOT_STAGGERABLE` in IN_POD); what a cap falling edge does while IN_POD is the Controller's (routed). A NONE with `loco_state` not IN_POD is not the pod: it is EXPOSED to the EXTERIOR (SE-3, Ship Body BDY-29). *(Web Map & Transit WM-17 and ASK-S1 answered the former Open Question 32 with a hold; the ruling D60 reverses that answer. Resolved 2026-10-27 — delegated ruling R6 (re-review; user delegated to best judgment): Suit's RUN reading stands and Web Map conforms on its side (WM-17b's HOLD reading deleted, ASK-S2 closed); Suit does not edit Web Map and does not claim the edit is done. The valve click plays only on the source transition edge: once on entering RESERVE and once on the disengage at arrival, never per run.)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R6)* *Criterion.* AC-SE-36a to 36f and AC-SE-94. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *Pillar.* P1.
269	
270	**SE-36. Co-op seams (record, do not build).** *Rule.* `repl_hint` is `SHARED_SUMMARY`, defined as exactly **`{locomotion_cap, vitals_state, cue_cold, cue_fog, cue_load, beam_shape, charge_band, carried_class}`** — no reserve value, no tool charges, no integrity number. A reading is private truth; a cue is public truth. The crew strip carries no vitals by default (the honest check is lighting a crewmate's visor). `revive` is dormant. Shape uniqueness is Co-op Session's; I-SUPPLY at four seats is SE-10's note. *Requested amendment (routed, not adopted on this GDD's authority):* the art-director finds the eight fields cannot drive all crewmate overlays — the summary lacks the seam jet (`cue_leak`) and the HEAVY back-frame (`stowed_heavy`), `cue_cold` must carry four values (none, vapour, rime level 1, rime level 2), and the systems-designer asks for a signed thermal cue so the heat side is not dropped; VS-B only (OQ-5). *Criterion.* AC-SE-37. *Pillar.* P1 (human channel).

272	**SE-37. No randomness, no scene tree.** *Rule.* Suit uses no RNG, no wall clock and no `delta` (H9): drain, ladder and cue thresholds are deterministic. Suit's hook, mutators and block contain no `Node` (H10). All values are int32-safe. *Criterion.* AC-SE-38. *Pillar.* P1 (replay determinism).

274	#### Group G — The interface Suit publishes
275	
276	**SE-38. The block schema (`suit.state`, per seat).** *Rule.* All fields are integers or plain-data dictionaries; no floats. One dictionary per seat, keyed by PlayerId.

The **closed restore reasons** are `SUIT_RESTORE_SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED`, `SUIT_RESTORE_FIELD_RANGE` (any field outside the table, including a `rung` not in 0..3, a `hold` or `rf_warmth` above its maximum or a `p_age` above `STAGGER_WINDOW_RUNS` + 1), `SUIT_RESTORE_STOWED_OVERFLOW` (a count above `stack_max`), `SUIT_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_DEF`, `SUIT_RESTORE_BEAM_SHAPE`, `SUIT_RESTORE_CARRY_MISMATCH`, `SUIT_RESTORE_SEAT_UNBOUND`, `SUIT_RESTORE_DATA_REV_UNKNOWN` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* and `SUIT_RESTORE_INSTANCE_FORM` (a held instance array of the wrong length or with a wrong element type) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. *Criterion.* AC-SE-35 and AC-SE-49a-c. *Pillar.* P5.

306	**SE-39. Run order inside `suit.vitals`.** *Rule.* Per run, for each bound seat in ascending PlayerId: (1) skip a seat that is unbound or DEAD (frozen); (2) resolve the room (SE-3) and step the pressure-drop window (D.12; may submit one `stagger`); (3) reconcile the respiration ledger (SE-5); (4) choose the breath source and draw or debit (SE-4); (5) apply the leak debit when `integrity_bp` is below `SUIT_LEAK_HP` (SE-22) — integrity as committed before this run, so a burn or arc crossing the threshold in step 8 of run n shows the seam jet on run n (derived on read) and first debits on run n+1, while a hit landed in P2 before run n debits in run n; (6) drain the cell from `emitter.state.lit` as of T-1 and call `force_off` at zero (SE-8); (7) step the thermal accumulator (SE-20); (8) apply the SCORCH burn and the arc damage (SE-22); (9) evaluate the three ladders (SE-17) on the post-step state; (10) derive the outputs (`locomotion_cap`, cue levels) and mark the dirty keys. Damage and credit mutators that land earlier in the tick (P2 apply, or another system's P3 hook) have already been applied to the block when the hook reads it. *Cost target (a model parameter, no budget exists in any GDD for Suit):* at most 0.05 ms per run in the Release export, O(bound seats × constant).

308	**SE-40. The published surface.** *Rule.* Every item below is Suit's, and **only these ids appear in any GDD example** (the kernel's `graph.propagate` example was copied by siblings; examples are read as contracts). *Commands:* exactly `equip_tool {slot: 1..6}`. *Reason codes Suit registers in its own namespace (closed; the kernel namespaces reasons per registering system, so Suit's `BUSY` and `NOT_ACTIONABLE` on `equip_tool` are distinct from Interaction's and the Controller's codes of the same name):* `EMPTY_SLOT`, `NOT_ACTIONABLE`, `BUSY`, `ALREADY_FULL` (read by Interaction's `top_up` validate), `STACK_FULL` (read by Interaction's pickup). `CHARGE_EMPTY` is the Emitter State's reason, read from Suit's charge; `OUT_OF_CHARGES` is Interaction's, read from Suit's counts. *Read views (pure; true values only):*

341	| `patch_integrity` | `(player_id, bp)` | capped at `SUIT_PATCH_CAP_BP`, never lowers | Interaction `begin_patch` on ACTOR_SELF (IA-17) |
342	| `replace_tool` | `(player_id, instance) -> discarded` | only when the held tool's charge is 0 | **dormant at MVP** (no suppressant in the kit, OQ-34); Interaction `pickup` at Vertical Slice *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* |

344	
345	*Calls Suit makes:* Graph `draw_air` (M15); Graph `withdraw_store` (M16) only inside V7's apply; Emitter `bind_beam` (E4, new game) and `force_off` (E5). *Retired names — do not use:* `consume_glowstick`, `stow`, `unstow`, `has_glowstick`, `equipped_tool`, `apply_harm`. *Diagnostics (names frozen 2026-10-27; read by the Debug Overlay as DIAGNOSTIC, dev builds only):* `suit_reserve_shortfall`, `suit_rung_limited{axis}`, `suit_cue_state{player}`, `suit_exo_bypass`; and, added 2026-10-27, `suit_restore_rescaled{from_rev, to_rev}` (not part of the frozen four; the Debug Overlay may subscribe). *Criterion.* AC-SE-39 (the guard-rail test: every published mutator changes only `suit.state`; the only registered command is `equip_tool`). *Pillar.* P1.
346	
347	**SE-41. Reserved parts — Interaction's reservation API, adopted.** *Rule.* A FULL repair job holds its part in a reserved state from the begin tick, so that the stock count and the weight cue cannot reveal whether a subject is truly damaged (a hallucinated-broken module would otherwise "spend no part" and a truly damaged one would, an oracle readable from the actor channel in about 100 ms at zero cost). Suit supplies the holder side with three Class B mutators, in addition to the SE-40 table: **`reserve_stowed(player_id, def_id, n) -> bool`** (moves `n` from the stowed count to a per-seat `reserved` bucket; returns false and changes nothing if the stowed count is below `n`), **`release_stowed(player_id, def_id, n)`** (returns reserved units to the stowed count) and **`consume_reserved(player_id, def_id, n)`** (destroys reserved units — the part is spent). A part in the reserved bucket is treated as having **left the pack from the begin tick, in both truth branches**: it is excluded from `stowed_count`, from `stowed_mass_g` and therefore from `cue_load`. Physically, the reserved part is at the work site, out of the pack, from the begin tick in both truth branches — so `cue_load` and the HEAVY back-frame remain true readings of what is on the back, never a suppressed cue (P1). The ledger of RESERVED and PAID records, their absolute `until` and `grace_until` ticks and the resume allowance are **Interaction's** (persisted in its own block); Suit persists only the per-seat reserved counts (SE-38), so a restore mid-job keeps the reservation and reintroduces no oracle. `spend_stowed` remains for the glowstick throw. A pickup into a stack that has units reserved is bounded by `stack_max` over stowed plus reserved. *(Interaction's designed IA-18 carries the three names, which Suit adopts on the precedent that the second GDD adopts the first's text. The stage ruling's R20 list had only `spend_stowed` for "a part on the first productive FULL step"; the reservation supersedes that caller. Interaction's stated fallback if Suit refuses — keep the spend at the first productive step and accept a one-run oracle — is not taken.)* *Why.* P1 and P4: an oracle that answers "is this module truly damaged" for free defeats the cost rule that makes a hallucinated broken state falsifiable only by time or risk. *Rejected.* Spending at the first productive step only (the oracle); refunding on abort (a free probe). *Criterion.* AC-SE-40: reserve → read `stowed_count` and `cue_load` → both fall at the begin tick whether or not the subject is damaged; `release_stowed` and `consume_reserved` conserve the total. *Pillar.* P1, P4.

#### Group F — Seams

**SE-31. No stimuli pushed.** *Rule.* Suit pushes no noise or power stimuli to Attention in the MVP. Per-verb noise class lives in **Interaction's verb declarations**; Suit keeps no noise field of its own (the earlier idea of a Suit-side noise table is withdrawn so there is one table of record). The kernel's Interactions row 4 says Suit "pushes noise/power stimuli to Attention": that wording is a routed refresh (Cross-References). The top-up is a Graph stock withdrawal; whether Attention sees it is not relied on here. *Criterion.* AC-SE-32 (no call from Suit's code to an Attention intake). *Pillar.* P3.

**SE-32. Pause.** *Rule.* Nothing Suit registers carries `allowed_when_paused`; `equip_tool` and every mutator are rejected while paused. The Chart Table's beam-shape pick is a boot or new-game call, not a runtime command. *Rejected.* Paused equip (lets a solo player re-arm with time stopped mid-tell, against Pillar 2). *Criterion.* AC-SE-33. *Pillar.* P2.

**SE-33. Autosave seam (adopted: Save/Load's package).** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *Rule.* Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): accept Save/Load's package (OQ-13; Save/Load OQ-40 and OQ-41; D14 and D42): (a) "any bound seat `vitals_state ≥ CRITICAL`" is a **third soft-gate input** for the autosave (deferred up to `AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS`, registry 7200, then written RISKY, invisible to the player: no glyph) and is **also applied to `quit_risky`**; (b) a **fairness step-back**: `loop_hit` also fires when `T_downed − g_r.T < W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE`, independent of `risky`; (c) a **post-DOWNED refractory** of `W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE` ticks. Save/Load owns (a)-(c) and their draft criteria AC-SL-128 and AC-SL-129, which are promoted there. *Suit's half.* Suit supplies exactly one input, `view(player_id).vitals_state` (the worst of the three persisted rungs, derived on read, never saved), and changes nothing else; a derived `time_to_failure_runs` read is **not minted** (a STRAINED-yet-doomed seat, for example 31 s of reserve and a 40 s exit, is caught by the step-back (b), not by the gate). *Derivation of the window used by (b) and (c).* `W_MIN_WARNING_S` is the registry's 10 s and `TICK_RATE` is 60, so the window is 10 × 60 = **600 ticks**. It is the Graph's own fairness floor, and Suit's `SUIT_MIN_WARNING_S` (20 s, 1,200 ticks) is at least twice it (build assertion A1). A generation written inside the final 600 ticks before a DOWNED seat's `T_downed` would restore the player with less than the minimum warning, so the step-back skips it. *Worked example.* A seat is first cued at tick t0 and is DOWNED at t0 + 1,500 (25 s, the breath floor of D.11): an autosave written at t0 + 1,000 is 500 ticks before `T_downed`, inside the window, so `loop_hit` fires and the restore steps back past it; one written at t0 + 800 is 700 ticks before and is not stepped back. The second route into a doomed restore, a data retune making every saved restore fail, is closed on Suit's side by `data_rev` (SE-34, AC-SE-49). The event autosaves for weld, cut and module-cut (D17), the assembly-breach withholding (D54) and the fault loss window (D55) are Save/Load's and Assembly's. *Criterion.* AC-SE-34a and 34b. *Pillar.* P5.

**SE-34. Save, restore, derived values.** *Rule.* SL-15 items 1-12 apply: `supported_versions`; a plain-data `snapshot()` (no `Vector2i`, no `StringName` keys, no typed containers); a two-phase `restore` returning `(ok, reason, detail)`; **hard failure, never clamp** on an out-of-range field *(except the declared `data_rev` migration below)*; `default_state()`; `post_restore` sets every `prev_*` field to its current value (no spurious edge cue after a restore); explicit dirty keys (4.7 packed-array rule); restore-idempotent (`snapshot(restore(snapshot()))` byte-equal); PER_PLAYER keyed by PlayerId. The closed restore reasons are in SE-38. **Data revisions** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the block persists a block-level `data_rev` (the revision of `assets/data/suit/*.json`, bumped by hand for any retune of `R_BREATH`, `RESERVE_S`, `CELL_S`, `TL_MAX`, `RUNG_MIN_TICKS`, `HYPOX_FAIL_S`, `INTEG_FAIL_S` or `STAGGER_WINDOW_TICKS`), and `assets/data/suit/rev_history.json` keeps, for each past revision, the saved values of `R_BREATH`, `RESERVE_S`, `CELL_S`, `TL_MAX` and the derived hold maxima. A saved `data_rev` equal to the current one is restored strictly (an out-of-range field is `SUIT_RESTORE_FIELD_RANGE`, a defect or tampering). A saved `data_rev` **older** than the current and present in the history is a legitimate retune and is **rescaled, not failed**: `reserve_mgu` and `cell_ticks` keep their felt fraction (`new = floor(saved × RESERVE_MAX_now / RESERVE_MAX_saved)`, likewise `CELL_MAX_TICKS`), `thermal_load` and every `hold`, `rf_warmth` and `p_age` are reduced to the new maxima (the safe direction: a shorter counter only lengthens the tell), the diagnostic `suit_restore_rescaled` is emitted, and the restore succeeds. A saved `data_rev` newer than the build, or absent from the history, fails `SUIT_RESTORE_DATA_REV_UNKNOWN`. Without this path a data retune made every saved restore fail and left the player with no loadable save at the moment of death (the doomed-save risk of OQ-13's second route). The rescale is a declared migration, not a clamp; Save/Load confirms it is within SL-15 (OQ-45). **Instance decode** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*: in `post_restore` (the same place and mechanism as `SUIT_RESTORE_CARRY_MISMATCH`; Suit's `restore_after` is `[]` but `post_restore` runs after all blocks restore, CR-8) Suit decodes every held instance with `from_array(a, graph_step_no)`, `graph_step_no` being the restored Graph's absolute 10 Hz `step_no`; a wrong length or element type fails `SUIT_RESTORE_INSTANCE_FORM`, a `validate_instance` failure maps to `SUIT_RESTORE_FIELD_RANGE`, an unknown `def_id` stays `SUIT_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_DEF` and a count above `stack_max` stays `SUIT_RESTORE_STOWED_OVERFLOW`; live state is untouched and nothing is clamped. Derived values — `locomotion_cap`, `vitals_state`, cue levels, `held_mass_g`, `stowed_mass_g`, `cue_load`, the breath source — are computed on read and never saved. MVP death is restart from the last autosave: `suit.state` rolls back with the world and there is no PROFILE block in the MVP. *Criterion.* AC-SE-35 (SL-15 round trip, restore idempotence). *Pillar.* P5.

**SE-35. External stagger, DECOMP pull, pod.** *Stagger.* The Controller registers the `SYSTEM`-origin command type `stagger {actor}` (registry `stagger`; Player Controller PC-1 b: `coalesce NONE`, `max_age_ticks` 120, no player binding, rejected `NOT_STAGGERABLE` in DOWNED, DEAD or IN_POD, Applied without extending the lock in STAGGERED); the former CONFLICT is closed, 2026-10-27. Suit submits one on a two-band pressure drop inside `STAGGER_WINDOW_TICKS` `[PH]` (dormant at MVP: no locked fixture fires it; the specified interface stays and is tested on synthetic traces; OQ-38) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, evaluated by **D.12** (the one normative statement of the trigger): the occupant's `band_p` index (NORMAL 0, LOW 1, DECOMP 2, VACUUM 3) must rise by 2 or more between a sample taken at most `STAGGER_WINDOW_TICKS` earlier and the current run, **in the same compartment**. A compartment change (a door crossing, the SE-3 NONE-to-EXPOSED switch, leaving IN_POD, the first run after a bind) re-anchors the window and never counts, so a player who walks into a vented room by choice is not input-locked for it, while a pressure fall inside the room they stand in is; one stagger per event; the two window ages are persisted (SE-38) so a restore mid-window replays the same trigger; the DECOMP cue plays as well, and a cap falling edge still staggers through the Controller's own rule. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *Pull.* Cue only (a lean, draught audio, dust); no displacement ("a stagger is animation plus input lock, never an impulse"). *Pod* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* (D60 reverses the former hold). Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): statuses run in the pod, and a death in the pod is the Controller's DEAD. While the Controller's `loco_state` is IN_POD, Suit runs the full SE-39 sequence for the seat against the pod cabin rule of SE-3 (i) (POD_RUN): **no `draw_air` call** (the pod's section is dormant and never breathed, Web Map & Transit WM-5, WM-17); the breath source is RESERVE and then NONE; the reserve drains `R_BREATH` per run; the cell drains while the beam is lit; the thermal load relaxes against COMFORT with no gain; every hold counter advances; the cap, the cues and the marks follow the ladders as anywhere. `pending_draw_mgu` is 0 in the pod, so no shortfall can arise: `breath_starved` stays 0 and no GASP cue fires across a leg (Web Map WM-17's required criterion holds by construction). A seat that reaches FAILED in the pod is DOWNED and then DEAD by the Controller's own rule (`DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS`); Suit special-cases nothing and holds nothing. What a leg costs, and when it can kill, is derived in D.1 (a nominal leg of 945 ticks spends 157 runs x 300 = 47,100 mGU, 15.7 s of the 90 s reserve, with the remainder of 3 ticks carried, so 157 or 158 runs; a pod death needs a leg of at least 250 runs, 25 s, so it is unreachable at the registry defaults) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R6)*. The `stagger` trigger cannot fire in the pod (D.12: `band_p` is NORMAL there by rule, and the Controller rejects `stagger` as `NOT_STAGGERABLE` in IN_POD); what a cap falling edge does while IN_POD is the Controller's (routed). A NONE with `loco_state` not IN_POD is not the pod: it is EXPOSED to the EXTERIOR (SE-3, Ship Body BDY-29). *(Web Map & Transit WM-17 and ASK-S1 answered the former Open Question 32 with a hold; the ruling D60 reverses that answer. Resolved 2026-10-27 — delegated ruling R6 (re-review; user delegated to best judgment): Suit's RUN reading stands and Web Map conforms on its side (WM-17b's HOLD reading deleted, ASK-S2 closed); Suit does not edit Web Map and does not claim the edit is done. The valve click plays only on the source transition edge: once on entering RESERVE and once on the disengage at arrival, never per run.)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R6)* *Criterion.* AC-SE-36a to 36f and AC-SE-94. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *Pillar.* P1.

**SE-36. Co-op seams (record, do not build).** *Rule.* `repl_hint` is `SHARED_SUMMARY`, defined as exactly **`{locomotion_cap, vitals_state, cue_cold, cue_fog, cue_load, beam_shape, charge_band, carried_class}`** — no reserve value, no tool charges, no integrity number. A reading is private truth; a cue is public truth. The crew strip carries no vitals by default (the honest check is lighting a crewmate's visor). `revive` is dormant. Shape uniqueness is Co-op Session's; I-SUPPLY at four seats is SE-10's note. *Requested amendment (routed, not adopted on this GDD's authority):* the art-director finds the eight fields cannot drive all crewmate overlays — the summary lacks the seam jet (`cue_leak`) and the HEAVY back-frame (`stowed_heavy`), `cue_cold` must carry four values (none, vapour, rime level 1, rime level 2), and the systems-designer asks for a signed thermal cue so the heat side is not dropped; VS-B only (OQ-5). *Criterion.* AC-SE-37. *Pillar.* P1 (human channel).

**SE-37. No randomness, no scene tree.** *Rule.* Suit uses no RNG, no wall clock and no `delta` (H9): drain, ladder and cue thresholds are deterministic. Suit's hook, mutators and block contain no `Node` (H10). All values are int32-safe. *Criterion.* AC-SE-38. *Pillar.* P1 (replay determinism).

#### Group G — The interface Suit publishes

**SE-38. The block schema (`suit.state`, per seat).** *Rule.* All fields are integers or plain-data dictionaries; no floats. One dictionary per seat, keyed by PlayerId.

| Field | Type | Range | Persisted | Dirty key (bucket) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `reserve_mgu` | int | 0..`RESERVE_MAX_MGU` | yes | `S/<PlayerId>` on a 5 % bucket of the maximum, on the engage edge and the warn edge |
| `breath_src` | int | 0 ROOM / 1 RESERVE / 2 GASP / 3 NONE | yes | on change |
| `breath_src_change_seq` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: D.10)* | int | 0..65535 | yes (so a restore is never an edge; presenters adopt the value silently) | on change (with `breath_src`) |
| `pending_draw_mgu` | int | 0..`R_BREATH` (the breath request only; the total asked of the Graph is this plus `pending_extra_mgu`, 0..`R_BREATH` + `TOPUP_PASSIVE_MGU_PER_RUN`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | yes | none (internal) |
| `breath_starved` | int | 0..1 | yes | on change |
| `pending_extra_mgu` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: PASSIVE credit term)* | int | 0..`TOPUP_PASSIVE_MGU_PER_RUN`; 0 in VERB mode | yes | none (internal) |
| `cell_ticks` | int | 0..`CELL_MAX_TICKS` | yes | 5 % bucket, the warn edge and the empty edge |
| `thermal_load` | int | `-TL_MAX`..`+TL_MAX` | yes | on a rung change or a cue-level change |
| `integrity_bp` | int | 0..`SUIT_HP_FULL` | yes | 250 bp bucket (the Graph's quantum) |
| `rung_breath`, `rung_warmth`, `rung_integrity` | int | 0..3 | yes | on change |

**SE-39. Run order inside `suit.vitals`.** *Rule.* Per run, for each bound seat in ascending PlayerId: (1) skip a seat that is unbound or DEAD (frozen); (2) resolve the room (SE-3) and step the pressure-drop window (D.12; may submit one `stagger`); (3) reconcile the respiration ledger (SE-5); (4) choose the breath source and draw or debit (SE-4); (5) apply the leak debit when `integrity_bp` is below `SUIT_LEAK_HP` (SE-22) — integrity as committed before this run, so a burn or arc crossing the threshold in step 8 of run n shows the seam jet on run n (derived on read) and first debits on run n+1, while a hit landed in P2 before run n debits in run n; (6) drain the cell from `emitter.state.lit` as of T-1 and call `force_off` at zero (SE-8); (7) step the thermal accumulator (SE-20); (8) apply the SCORCH burn and the arc damage (SE-22); (9) evaluate the three ladders (SE-17) on the post-step state; (10) derive the outputs (`locomotion_cap`, cue levels) and mark the dirty keys. Damage and credit mutators that land earlier in the tick (P2 apply, or another system's P3 hook) have already been applied to the block when the hook reads it. *Cost target (a model parameter, no budget exists in any GDD for Suit):* at most 0.05 ms per run in the Release export, O(bound seats × constant).

**SE-40. The published surface.** *Rule.* Every item below is Suit's, and **only these ids appear in any GDD example** (the kernel's `graph.propagate` example was copied by siblings; examples are read as contracts). *Commands:* exactly `equip_tool {slot: 1..6}`. *Reason codes Suit registers in its own namespace (closed; the kernel namespaces reasons per registering system, so Suit's `BUSY` and `NOT_ACTIONABLE` on `equip_tool` are distinct from Interaction's and the Controller's codes of the same name):* `EMPTY_SLOT`, `NOT_ACTIONABLE`, `BUSY`, `ALREADY_FULL` (read by Interaction's `top_up` validate), `STACK_FULL` (read by Interaction's pickup). `CHARGE_EMPTY` is the Emitter State's reason, read from Suit's charge; `OUT_OF_CHARGES` is Interaction's, read from Suit's counts. *Read views (pure; true values only):*

*Calls Suit makes:* Graph `draw_air` (M15); Graph `withdraw_store` (M16) only inside V7's apply; Emitter `bind_beam` (E4, new game) and `force_off` (E5). *Retired names — do not use:* `consume_glowstick`, `stow`, `unstow`, `has_glowstick`, `equipped_tool`, `apply_harm`. *Diagnostics (names frozen 2026-10-27; read by the Debug Overlay as DIAGNOSTIC, dev builds only):* `suit_reserve_shortfall`, `suit_rung_limited{axis}`, `suit_cue_state{player}`, `suit_exo_bypass`; and, added 2026-10-27, `suit_restore_rescaled{from_rev, to_rev}` (not part of the frozen four; the Debug Overlay may subscribe). *Criterion.* AC-SE-39 (the guard-rail test: every published mutator changes only `suit.state`; the only registered command is `equip_tool`). *Pillar.* P1.

**SE-41. Reserved parts — Interaction's reservation API, adopted.** *Rule.* A FULL repair job holds its part in a reserved state from the begin tick, so that the stock count and the weight cue cannot reveal whether a subject is truly damaged (a hallucinated-broken module would otherwise "spend no part" and a truly damaged one would, an oracle readable from the actor channel in about 100 ms at zero cost). Suit supplies the holder side with three Class B mutators, in addition to the SE-40 table: **`reserve_stowed(player_id, def_id, n) -> bool`** (moves `n` from the stowed count to a per-seat `reserved` bucket; returns false and changes nothing if the stowed count is below `n`), **`release_stowed(player_id, def_id, n)`** (returns reserved units to the stowed count) and **`consume_reserved(player_id, def_id, n)`** (destroys reserved units — the part is spent). A part in the reserved bucket is treated as having **left the pack from the begin tick, in both truth branches**: it is excluded from `stowed_count`, from `stowed_mass_g` and therefore from `cue_load`. Physically, the reserved part is at the work site, out of the pack, from the begin tick in both truth branches — so `cue_load` and the HEAVY back-frame remain true readings of what is on the back, never a suppressed cue (P1). The ledger of RESERVED and PAID records, their absolute `until` and `grace_until` ticks and the resume allowance are **Interaction's** (persisted in its own block); Suit persists only the per-seat reserved counts (SE-38), so a restore mid-job keeps the reservation and reintroduces no oracle. `spend_stowed` remains for the glowstick throw. A pickup into a stack that has units reserved is bounded by `stack_max` over stowed plus reserved. *(Interaction's designed IA-18 carries the three names, which Suit adopts on the precedent that the second GDD adopts the first's text. The stage ruling's R20 list had only `spend_stowed` for "a part on the first productive FULL step"; the reservation supersedes that caller. Interaction's stated fallback if Suit refuses — keep the spend at the first productive step and accept a one-run oracle — is not taken.)* *Why.* P1 and P4: an oracle that answers "is this module truly damaged" for free defeats the cost rule that makes a hallucinated broken state falsifiable only by time or risk. *Rejected.* Spending at the first productive step only (the oracle); refunding on abort (a free probe). *Criterion.* AC-SE-40: reserve → read `stowed_count` and `cue_load` → both fall at the begin tick whether or not the subject is damaged; `release_stowed` and `consume_reserved` conserve the total. *Pillar.* P1, P4.
